scope: Proposition 2.2 (Affine 2-to-1 Games Theorem) of the manuscript “A Direct Proof of Optimal Max-Cut Hardness” (preprints/A-Direct-Proof-of-Optimal-Max-Cut-Hardness-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 102 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 32a11e793f6e379c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every constant b ∈ (0, 1) there is an integer n ≥ 1 such that, for every constant a ∈ (0, 1 − b), the following promise problem is NP-hard. Its input is a weighted bipartite game with vertex sets X, Y , respective label sets Fn+1 2 , Fn 2 , and a surjective affine map πe : Fn+1 2 −→ Fn 2 on each edge e = (x, y). An edge is satisfied when πe(λX(x)) = λY (y). The promise cases are YES : Val(G) ≥ 1 − a, NO : Val(G) ≤ b. The integer n depends on b alone. For fixed a, b, the reduction is deterministic and has polynomial running time and output size.
